hook_text: 3/4, 5/8 or 7/10 — who ate the most lunch? Cut it into 40 pieces.
clip_script: Compare three quarters, five eighths and seven tenths. The denominators are four, eight and ten; their LCM is forty. Three quarters is thirty fortieths. Five eighths is twenty-five fortieths. Seven tenths is twenty-eight fortieths. Now compare numerators: twenty-five, twenty-eight, thirty. From smallest to largest: five eighths, seven tenths, three quarters.
visual_style: Three lunch boxes cut into quarters, eighths and tenths; each is re-cut into 40 tiny squares and the eaten squares are counted side by side.
pacing: Quick setup, re-cutting animation, snap to the order.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to simplify any fraction step by step.
